# Module 9: After-sales, warranty and maintenance

*Every callback starts with the full history, and the close-out writes itself.*

**Who does it in a small business:** Owner, service coordinator, techs.

## The typical process

Every business does it a bit differently. This is the common shape we see.

| # | Step | What happens | Tools | Where time goes |
|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Callback or fault | Email, phone, a ticket | Outlook, Phone |  |
| 2 | Find the history | What was supplied, past visits, the drawings | Excel, SharePoint, Field app | slow |
| 3 | Decide: fix by phone or visit | Most visits are booked without the history | Phone |  |
| 4 | Visit and report | Photos, notes, a report written up later | Field app, Word, Voice note | copy-paste |
| 5 | Close out | Report sent, invoice, warranty or credit | PDF, Xero | slow |
| 6 | Maintenance and renewals | Service contracts, asset lists, renewals | Excel, Word | slow |

## Where the time goes

From businesses APG has audited, anonymised. Hours are staff estimates, not measurements.

- Every callback treated as new; repeat faults go unseen
- In one business, two of three trips in a week could have been avoided
- Close-out paperwork: about 5 h a week, more work than the repair
- Maintenance contracts and renewals: about 26 h a week for one person

## Step 1: the intake

"How we do it" (planned): Map what happens after the job: how callbacks come in, what history you check, how you close out.

It hands back your own version of the map above, with your tools and your hours, then suggests which skill to build first.

## The skills

- **Site history** (connected): Everything supplied and every past visit, before anyone goes
- **Spoken close-out** (connected): One voice debrief becomes the report, photos and invoice notes
- **Renewal builder** (drop in a file): Last year's contract and asset list turned into this year's
